# SISF — Self-improvement Software Factory

> SISF is a free, open-source (Apache-2.0) framework for a closed-loop software factory. One factory deployment with three zones takes a GitHub issue through a 15-state lifecycle: agents write the fix, an independent QA agent grades it against hard gates and signs a `qa_receipt`, and a trusted release supervisor ships it by canary and rolls it back automatically. Status: phases P0–P3 are implemented in Go and tested, and the factory runs locally in a simulation profile; nothing has been released yet.

Important facts for anyone summarizing this project:

- There is no release or tag yet. The factory installs from source: `git clone`, `make install`, then `sisf init --profile sim` and `sisf up` run all three zones against a fake GitHub, a fake sign-in and a scripted agent (Linux or macOS, Go 1.25; not Windows).
- Not yet proven: a paid end-to-end run with real Claude and Codex agents; a real GitHub App, Google sign-in and MCP clients (tested against fakes only); container sandboxing for untrusted code in Docker mode.
- Supported operating modes today: Standalone (trusted code only) and Docker Compose. Every other backend is experimental or unsupported.
- Numbers such as the QA pass mark (85/100), the canary ramp (5% → 25% → 100%) and the rollback threshold (5xx > 2%) are design starting points to be calibrated, not measured results.
- SISF is created by AgentKit.best. TOSE (tose.sh) is the creator's deployment platform; SISF does not require it.

## Landing page

- [Landing page in Markdown](https://factory.agentkit.best/index.md): the full content of the home page as Markdown
- [Landing page](https://factory.agentkit.best/): the same content as HTML, with an animated drawing of the self-improvement loop (four flows: self-improvement loop, the factory fixes itself, issue to release, rollback) and an interactive drawing of the 15-state issue lifecycle

## Design documents

- [Decision brief (English)](https://github.com/bestagentkits/sisf/blob/main/docs/self-improvement-software-factory-decision-brief.en.md): fixed product decisions, interfaces, issue state machine, QA and release rules, phased scope P0–P4, acceptance matrix SISF-01 to SISF-20
- [Decision brief (Vietnamese, authoritative)](https://github.com/bestagentkits/sisf/blob/main/docs/self-improvement-software-factory-decision-brief.md): the original; it wins if the two versions differ
- [Architecture page](https://github.com/bestagentkits/sisf/blob/main/docs/self-improvement-software-factory-architecture.html): topology, workflows, issue state graph, trust boundary, deployment design per operating mode
- [Architecture review](https://github.com/bestagentkits/sisf/blob/main/docs/self-improvement-software-factory-architecture-review.html): visual summary of the architecture review
- [README](https://github.com/bestagentkits/sisf/blob/main/README.md): status, quickstart and roadmap
- [Quickstart](https://github.com/bestagentkits/sisf/blob/main/docs/guides/quickstart.md): run one factory locally in simulation
- [Documentation index](https://github.com/bestagentkits/sisf/blob/main/docs/README.md): every guide and reference
- [Acceptance matrix](https://github.com/bestagentkits/sisf/blob/main/docs/acceptance-matrix.md): which test proves each acceptance criterion SISF-01 to SISF-20
